newsitem.title: USA: Dow Corning posts 20 percent rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Dow Corning posts 20 percent rise in profits.

text.p: Dow Corning Corp. said Tuesday that its profits expanded by almost 20 percent in the third quarter as cost controls helped it recover from a spring sales slump.
The company, which is jointly owned by Dow Chemical Co. and Corning Inc., said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 grew to $56.4 million from $47.3 million.
Dow Corning, based in Midland, Mich., said its global sales increased by 3.2 percent to $644.3 million from $624.3 million as they recovered from a second-quarter decline.

"Dow Corning experienced good third-quarter profit growth when compared with the same period last year, despite relatively modest sales growth," Chief Financial Officer John Churchfield said in a statement.
"This profit performance is largely due to tight control over operating expenses, and higher interest income."
The company said its net income for the first nine months of the year was $160.3 million, compared with a $70.2 million loss in the year-ago period.
The company noted that its year-ago income was reduced by a $351 million charge related to costs associated with its silicone breast implant products, which are the subject of ongoing litigation.
Sales for the nine months edged up 0.8 percent to $1.89 billion from the $1.88 billion.
